content: Clarithromycin significantly interacts with various drugs by altering their metabolism, primarily through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, as well as P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. These interactions can lead to increased drug levels, enhanced effects, or heightened toxicity, necessitating careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or the use of alternative therapies. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Clarithromycin and Natural Progesterone: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 2. Clarithromycin and Promazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Clarithromycin and Promethazine: Similar to promazine, both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin and Propafenone: Clarithromycin raises propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Clarithromycin and Protamines: Clarithromycin increases the effects of protamines by reducing their metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Clarithromycin and Protriptyline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Clarithromycin and Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6): Clarithromycin decreases pyridoxine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin and Quazepam: Clarithromycin increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Clarithromycin and Quetiapine: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin and Quinidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Clarithromycin and Vonoprazan: Vonoprazan increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor. 12. Clarithromycin and Quinine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin and Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases clarithromycin levels by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Clarithromycin and Quizartinib: Clarithromycin increases quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended due to QT prolongation risk. 15. Clarithromycin and Rabeprazole: Clarithromycin increases rabeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Clarithromycin and Ramelteon: Clarithromycin increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin and Ranolazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Clarithromycin and Regorafenib: Co-administration is contraindicated as clarithromycin increases regorafenib levels while reducing exposure to its active metabolites (M-2 and M-5). 19. Clarithromycin and Repaglinide: Clarithromycin increases repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and Selpercatinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Clarithromycin and Selumetinib: Clarithromycin increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce selumetinib dosage if co-administration is unavoidable. 22. Clarithromycin and Sertraline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin and Sevoflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin and Sildenafil: Clarithromycin increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin and Silodosin: Clarithromycin increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and Rivaroxaban: Clarithromycin increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid co-administration in patients with renal impairment (CrCl 15–80 mL/min). 27. Clarithromycin and Roflumilast: Clarithromycin increases roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin and Romidepsin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin and Rosiglitazone: Clarithromycin increases rosiglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor glucose levels closely due to the risk of hypoglycemia. 30. Clarithromycin and Rosuvastatin: Clarithromycin increases rosuvastatin toxicity by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages if clinically indicated. 32. Clarithromycin and Ruxolitinib: Clarithromycin increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib in patients with adequate platelet counts or avoid use in those with low platelet counts. 33. Clarithromycin and Sacubitril/Valsartan: Clarithromycin increases valsartan levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Monitor closely for increased systemic exposure. 34. Clarithromycin and Salmeterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Clarithromycin and Saxagliptin: Clarithromycin increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Clarithromycin and Seladelpar: Clarithromycin increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. 37. Clarithromycin and Silodosin: Clarithromycin increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Clarithromycin and Rilpivirine: Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to QT prolongation risk. 39. Clarithromycin and Rimegepant: Clarithromycin increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin and Riociguat: Clarithromycin increases riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin and Ripretinib: Clarithromycin increases ripretinib levels and its active metabolite (DP-5439) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely due to the risk of adverse reactions. 42. Clarithromycin and Ritonavir: Clarithromycin increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin and Rifabutin: Clarithromycin increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for toxicity. 44. Clarithromycin and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin and Rufinamide: Rufinamide decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 46. Clarithromycin and Selpercatinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 47. Clarithromycin and Sertraline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 48. Clarithromycin and Sevoflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin and Sildenafil: Clarithromycin increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Clarithromycin and Silodosin: Clarithromycin increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug-drug interactions when prescribing clarithromycin, as it can significantly alter the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of co-administered medications.
